title: The children in the field
note: Saying 21 also includes a thief saying and a harvest image with related Gospel passages.

title: The lion and the human
note: The paradox has disputed meaning; translations and possible emendations differ.

title: The five trees
note: The five trees are an image whose interpretation is uncertain.

title: Protecting a brother like the eye
note: Thomas compares care for a brother with protecting the pupil of the eye.

title: The world and a corpse
note: Compare Thomas 80, which uses body rather than corpse; their wording differs.

title: The Samaritan and the lamb
note: Jesus and the disciples discuss the lamb; this is not the Good Samaritan story.

title: Bringing forth what is within
note: The saying contains bracketed words; the image and its interpretation are disputed.

title: The empty well
note: The speaker and the meaning of the crowded well are unclear in the saying.

title: Light, wood and stone
note: Thomas combines a statement about light with finding the speaker in wood and stone.

title: The world and a body
note: Compare Thomas 56, which uses corpse rather than body; their wording differs.

title: Likeness and images
note: The saying contrasts a visible likeness with images that came into being earlier; interpretation is uncertain.

title: Body and soul depending
note: The saying describes dependence among body and soul; its interpretation is not explained.

title: Father, mother and the true Mother
note: Words and a clause are damaged or reconstructed; the source marks them with brackets and a gap.

title: Drinking from the speaker’s mouth
note: The saying joins drinking, becoming alike and the revelation of what is hidden.

title: Flesh and soul depending
note: The saying presents mutual dependence of flesh and soul as a pair of woes.
